What is Agent Kernel? Agent Kernel is a framework-agnostic runtime designed to streamline the entire lifecycle of AI agent development. articles.title: Your phone is a better astrology computer than a server
articles.excerpt: TL;DR: A birth chart is deterministic. Same inputs, same output, forever. So I stopped asking "how do I build this API?" and started asking "what actually needs to leave the device?" The answer: much…
articles.body: TL;DR: A birth chart is deterministic. Same inputs, same output, forever. So I stopped asking "how do I build this API?" and started asking "what actually needs to leave the device?" The answer: much less than I expected. Astrology apps have a shape, and the shape is: thin client, fat backend . The phone collects a birth date and sends it somewhere. Something comes back. The phone draws it. I built JanamJyot the other way round, and the interesting part wasn't the astrology. It was discovering how much of what I assumed needed a server didn't. 🧭 Start with what has to be true A birth chart is deterministic. Date, time and place in; planetary positions, lagna, nakshatra, divisional charts and the dasha timeline out. Same inputs, same outputs, forever.
articles.author: Vansh Kashyap

articles.title: Our robots.txt is 781 lines, and 688 of them are one rule written 344 times
articles.excerpt: Open cogniprep.app/robots.txt. It is 781 lines and 22,827 bytes. Google's limit is 500 KiB, so there is plenty of headroom, but this is not a file anyone typed. The counts, if you want to check them a…
articles.body: Open cogniprep.app/robots.txt . It is 781 lines and 22,827 bytes. Google's limit is 500 KiB, so there is plenty of headroom, but this is not a file anyone typed. The counts, if you want to check them against your own read of it: count Allow: lines 34 Disallow: lines 740 Disallow: lines starting /games/ 688 user-agent groups 2 Everything is doubled because there are two groups, so the real numbers are 17 allows and 370 disallows, emitted twice. And 344 of those 370 are individual game routes. This post is about why a file would ever look like that. It is a TypeScript module, not a text file CogniPrep is Next.js, so robots.txt comes from app/robots.ts , a function that returns an object.

articles.title: Install Underpeaks Core: A Free, Self-Hosted Headless CMS for Flutter and Next.js
articles.excerpt: If you've ever built the same app for web and mobile, you know the tax: two codebases, two sets of backend glue code, and one data model you keep in sync by hand. Change a field, update it in both pla…
articles.body: If you've ever built the same app for web and mobile, you know the tax: two codebases, two sets of backend glue code, and one data model you keep in sync by hand. Change a field, update it in both places, miss one, ship a bug. Underpeaks Core is a free, open-source, self-hosted headless CMS built to get rid of that. You define your data model once, and it gives you a backend, a content editor and a REST API. It can also generate working Flutter and Next.js apps from the same model. It's compiled, not AI-generated, so the same model always gives you the same code. The video above shows the whole install. Here's the written version, so you can follow along or come back to it. What you need Node.js and npm Git A database: Supabase, PostgreSQL, MySQL, MongoDB or Firebase.
